agency.name: Office of Workers' Compensation, Division of Industrial Affairs, Delaware Department of Labor

ttd.basisLabel: Gross average weekly wage before taxes
ttd.rateText: 66 2/3% of the injured employee's wages, not more than 66 2/3% of the state average weekly wage announced by the Secretary of Labor for the last calendar year (19 Del. C. § 2324).
ttd.minText: Minimum is 22 2/9% of the state average weekly wage; an employee earning less receives the full amount of his or her wages (19 Del. C. § 2324).
ttd.periodLabel: effective July 1, 2026 (state AWW for calendar year 2025 = $1,444.07)

waiting.text: Compensation is paid beginning with the fourth day of incapacity; if incapacity extends to 7 days or more, including the day of injury, compensation is paid from the first day. Medical, hearing/vision loss and funeral benefits are paid from day one (19 Del. C. § 2321).

ttdDuration.text: Total disability compensation is paid during the continuance of total disability, with no fixed week cap (19 Del. C. § 2324); partial disability is limited to 300 weeks (19 Del. C. § 2325).

ppd.text: Permanent injuries are paid at 66 2/3% of wages for scheduled periods regardless of earning power, e.g. hand 220 weeks, arm 250, foot 160, leg 250, thumb 75, index finger 50 weeks; partial loss of use is paid proportionally (19 Del. C. § 2326).

facts.text: The maximum rate changes every July 1 and equals two-thirds of the prior calendar year's state average weekly wage, derived from employers in the state unemployment insurance system.
The Office of Workers' Compensation publishes daily rates for partial weeks: $137.54 for day 1 up to $962.72 for day 7 at the July 1, 2026 maximum.
If an employee's wages are below the minimum rate (22 2/9% of the state AWW), the employee receives his or her full wages as compensation (19 Del. C. § 2324).
Unless the employer has actual knowledge, notice of injury must be given within 90 days after the accident or no compensation is due until notice is given (19 Del. C. § 2341).
